---
title: "Companion curriculum"
subtitle: "The teaching modules of the Europeanisation case study"
---

The workshop is built around one exercise: you reproduce a recorded result, vary the analysis behind it, declare one analysis before you run it, and read your result against those of the class. Here the exercise is taught on the Europeanisation and the economy case study, which is presented in full on the [background page](../background.qmd). In it, a published claim linking a country's economic performance to the terms in which its citizens frame the European Union is examined on a panel of 270 country-years built from sixteen Eurobarometer waves. Since a single day has room for that exercise and little else, the skills surrounding it are taught in the ten modules listed below, which range from R and the IDE to a reanalysis that you can deposit and register. Each module is self-contained, which allows you to take the one you need and leave the rest.

Every module is written for this case study, and those that run code compute their numbers from the case-study files in `data/` when the page is built. A module can thus be read as a worked analysis as well as an explanation, and you can check each number against your own output. The models that require the respondents themselves, whose Eurobarometer files may not be passed on, were fitted once on the licensed files, and the modules display the saved output of these models beside the code that produced it.

None of the modules is required for the full-day format, which runs in full without any module and with no account to create. The pages in the full-day format point to some modules as preparation, to others as the slower companion of one of its parts, and to the rest as reading for afterwards.

The modules fall into the three groups below. The first comprises the computational tools with which an analysis is written, the second the data and the public records that allow others to find an analysis and run it again, and the third the statistical methods by which the case study is analysed. Within each group the modules are arranged roughly in the order of what each one presupposes of the reader.

## Tools {#sec-tools}

The modules on the tools are hosted on the workshop's umbrella website: [Getting started with R](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/r.html) with its [second](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/r-further.html) and [third](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/r-functions.html) parts, [Positron and other IDEs](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/ide.html), [Quarto documents](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/quarto.html) and [Git and GitHub](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/git-github.html), while the [setup page](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html) there explains how to install R, Quarto and an IDE, with the [setup help](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/help.html) beside it. Two modules here apply the same tools to the panel and the workspace of the Europeanisation case study:

- [R on the country-year panel](intro-r.qmd) – the files of the case study and the routes by which they arrive, the grammar of graphics on the panel of the case study, and reading its specification curve.
- [The workspace in the IDE](ide.qmd) – six steps through the workspace of the case study, in whichever IDE you chose.

## Data and sharing {#sec-sharing}

- [Social science data sources](data-sources.qmd) – the three routes by which data reach a researcher, a map of the archives and series, and the routes of the case study from GESIS, the World Bank, Eurostat and the OSF.
- [Building the analysis file](data-management.qmd) – the steps of a build, worked through for the country-year panel of the case study from the sixteen Eurobarometer waves and checked against the committed files.
- [Reproducibility repositories](repositories.qmd) – what a repository does, the SCORE dossier and the records of the SCORE robustness study (Aczel et al. 2026) on the paper, the OSF after 2026, registrations, and depositing a reanalysis of your own.

## Methods {#sec-methods}

- [Panel data](panel-data.qmd) – the estimators of the country-year panel: the linear model, clustered standard errors with few clusters, the two fixed-effects designs, random effects and the within–between model.
- [Causal graphs and adjustment sets](dags.qmd) – what a causal graph commits you to, confounders, mediators and colliders, the graph of the case study and its adjustment set, and what fixed effects cannot absorb.
- [Scale construction](measurement.qmd) – the thirteen items from which every outcome of the menu is built, how they hang together, their factor structure and reliability, the outcome decisions of the curve, and the rules of the menu for the respondents who mention no item, with multiple imputation and a sensitivity band.
- [Meta-analysis](meta-analysis.qmd) – the common scale of the robustness study, the five analysts of the case study on it, the two-way slope as a weighted average of the country slopes, and other studies of many analysts.
- [The multiverse and its critics](multiverse.qmd) – where multiverse analysis came from, the debate of 2025–26, robustness against replicability, and the curve of the case study with its pruned menu and its displays of heterogeneity.

The reading on what a test of the curve as a whole can and cannot establish, presented with [the specification curve](../curve.qmd#inference) of the case study, belongs with these modules without being one of them.
